biography.plain_text: Joseph Wesley was an American businessman who founded Tradesmen International, a staffing company supplying skilled construction workers. A Cleveland native and Army veteran, he first ran RIC Electric before building the national recruitment business. Private equity investors later acquired the company, which had grown from his experience managing an electrical contractor.

long_biography.plain_text:
A shortage of electricians on a NASA project helped staffing entrepreneur Joseph Wesley devise his staffing model. He arranged additional labour for the contract, completed the work profitably and wrote a business plan that evening. Tradesmen employed the craftworkers itself, providing benefits while matching them to contractors whose workload changed from project to project.

Wesley and his wife, Kimberly, also gave USD 10 million to University Hospitals to establish the Wesley Center for Immunotherapy. The gift supported research and greater treatment capacity at a hospital whose cell therapy facility manufactured CAR-T and other cell-based therapies for clinical trials.
